results.cause: Likely cause: on the "cap / floor:screen" Save action, a validation error becomes visible shortly after each Save click, and the events show the user editing Notional and Counterparty between attempts without any error-cleared event, so the same error seems to persist across the three Save attempts; the Counterparty error is already visible on focus before the first Save, which suggests the error is not tied to the field being edited.
results.fix: Fix: On the "cap / floor:screen" form, render the validation message inline beside the specific invalid input (Notional and Counterparty) instead of a generic error after the Save button, and clear that message when the input changes, so the Save button's error state reflects the current field values.

results.cause: Likely cause: on the cap / floor screen, each Save click (ids 325, 374, 423) is followed by a visible error event (app:52, app:66, app:80) about 300 to 500 ms later, and the user edits the Notional field before each retry (ids 350/351, 399/400), which suggests the Save validation fails on an input that is not identified in the error event.
results.fix: Fix: on the cap / floor screen, change the Save button's validation handler so that a failed save shows the error message inline beside the invalid field and moves focus to that field, instead of a generic visible error that does not name the field.

results.cause: Likely cause: on the cap / floor form, each Save click returns a visible error (app:52, app:66, app:80, each after a Save at 325, 374, 423), and each attempt then restarts with a return to the Notional field (focus 308, 347, 396, followed by keystrokes 351, 400), which suggests Notional is the field the validation is pointing at, though the events do not show the error text or which field it refers to.
results.fix: Fix: on the cap / floor form, validate the Notional input on blur and show its error message inline beneath the Notional field, so the problem is flagged before Save is clicked and the Save-time error no longer requires returning to Notional.

results.cause: Likely cause: after each Save click on the cap / floor screen, a visible error event fires, and the user then edits Trade Date, Counterparty, or Notional and clicks Save again, with the same error appearing again. The error seems to persist or re-trigger after the edits, and no event shows which field it refers to or that it cleared.
results.fix: Fix: On the cap / floor screen, make the Save button's validation error name the offending field inline next to Counterparty, Notional, or Trade Date, and clear that field's error as soon as its input changes, so a user can see which value Save is rejecting before retrying.

results.cause: Likely cause: on the cap / floor form, each Save click is followed by a loading overlay and then a visible error (app:38, app:45, app:52), and each time the user returns focus to the Notional input (325, 360, 409) before pressing Save again, so the Save-time error appears to be tied to the Notional entry, though the events do not name the field that failed validation.
results.fix: Fix: On the cap / floor form, change the Save-triggered error so it names the invalid field and moves focus to it, and show an inline error directly under the Notional input on blur so the problem is visible before Save is pressed.

results.cause: Likely cause: in all three sessions the user clicked the Apply span at nearly the same spot five times in about a second, and no navigation, error, overlay, or other state-change event follows those clicks before the next action several seconds later, so the button appears to give no immediate feedback.
results.fix: Fix: on the Apply button in the "ir swap:screen" screen, disable the control and show an in-progress indicator (or a "Applying..." label) on the first click, so repeat clicks are blocked and the response is visible right away.

results.cause: Likely cause: the Apply control gives no visible response after the first click, so the same spot is clicked again; in session S5360a38e, five Apply clicks at the same position (events 109, 115, 120, 125, 131) fall within about 0.8 s with no navigation, coverage, error, or state-change event between them.
results.fix: Fix: On the ir swap screen, disable the Apply button (the span at the Apply position) and show a pending indicator as soon as it is first clicked, keeping it disabled until the apply request resolves.

results.cause: Likely cause: in both windows, visible error events appear within about 60 to 200 ms of the first input into the "As Of Date" field (S65766c5e: input 9155 ms, errors 9212 and 9357 ms; S39f93c58: input 9852 ms, errors 9908 and 10065 ms), before the user moves on to Entity and Portfolio, so validation feedback on the date field may be interrupting the form.
results.fix: Fix: On the cashflow report form, make the "As Of Date" validation message render inline beside that field and run validation on blur or submit instead of on each keystroke, so the first typed value does not raise a visible error before the Portfolio field is reached.

results.cause: Likely cause: on the trade list screen, the rowgroup scroll container is scrolled down by 225 px and back up to 0 px repeatedly with no click, input, or filter event between reversals, which suggests the list has no in-place way to narrow or locate rows, so the user is scanning it by hand.
results.fix: Fix: on the trade list screen, add a search or filter input above the rowgroup scroll container (or a sticky header row inside it) so users can narrow rows without repeated scrolling up and down.

results.cause: Likely cause: the trade list's scrollable rowgroup shows only a short slice of rows at a time, so users scroll down to 225 and back to 0 repeatedly, with no clicks or typing between the reversals (scroll events 276 to 310 in Scdc0bc9d, and 289 to 324 in S8b09fbb0, both after navigation app:24 or app:42 to trade list:screen).
results.fix: Fix: On the trade list:screen, change the "Scroll container" rowgroup so it fills the available viewport height (for example, flex: 1 with min-height: 0 on the list wrapper), and add a sticky column header inside that container so rows can be reviewed without repeated scroll-to-top returns.

results.cause: Likely cause: a visible error appeared as the Counterparty field was focused (event 92:a107), and the user edited Counterparty and then left the ir swap form for Static Data about 1.2 s later without a save, though the error text is not captured so the exact reason cannot be confirmed.
results.fix: Fix: On the ir swap screen, check the Counterparty input's validation so it does not show an error state on focus, and where an error is shown, render its message beside the Counterparty field and record that message in the error event.

results.cause: Likely cause: in both windows, a visible error event fires within about 6-8 ms of the Counterparty field receiving focus (61:a65 at 3438 ms after focus at 3431 ms; 98:a104 at 7565 ms after focus at 7557 ms), before any keystroke in that field, so the field appears to be in an error state on arrival; in both sessions the user then moved to Static Data and navigated to counterparty:screen rather than continuing to edit the form.
results.fix: Fix: On the ir swap:screen form, change the Counterparty input so its validation error is not shown on focus; show the error only on blur or on save attempt, and check why the error is already set before the user types.

results.cause: Likely cause: On Ir Swap, the Counterparty textbox shows a visible error right after it gains focus (error events 61:a65 and 98:a104), and in both sessions the user then opens Static Data > Counterparty from the top menu (clicks 92 and 140), reaches counterparty:screen, and returns to Ir Swap after a save-success action (app:23:success, app:17:success). This suggests the Counterparty field needs a value that the user has to look up or create on the Counterparty screen, but the error gives no in-place path to it.
results.fix: Fix: On the Ir Swap screen, in the Counterparty textbox, render the validation message inline when the error appears and add a link beside it that opens the Counterparty list (or a picker/search) so the user can select a valid counterparty without navigating to Static Data > Counterparty and back.

results.cause: Likely cause: On the "ir swap:screen" form, a visible error event fires on the Counterparty input within about 5 ms of focus (focus 61 at 3224 ms, error 62:a64 at 3229 ms), before any typing in that field, and the user then types in Counterparty (68), moves to Notional (79), and leaves via the Static Data menu to "counterparty:screen" (92, app:13), so the form is left unsaved.
results.fix: Fix: On the "ir swap:screen" form, change the Counterparty input so its validation message is shown only after blur or submit (not on focus), and add an inline "Find or create counterparty" link beside the Counterparty field that opens Static Data in a new tab so the unsaved IR swap form is preserved.

results.cause: Likely cause: after a visible error appears on the Ir Swap form while the Counterparty field is being filled (error events 62:a64 and 50:a51/54:a56), users open Trades > Static Data and reach the Counterparty screen (navigation app:13 / app:30), then return to Ir Swap through the Trades tab (app:15 / app:32), which suggests the Counterparty value is not available inline on the Ir Swap form.
results.fix: Fix: On the Ir Swap screen, Counterparty input, add an inline counterparty search or picker that lists valid counterparties so users can select one without leaving for Trades > Static Data, and render the visible validation error next to the field that raised it with its field label.

results.cause: Likely cause: after the "Hedge Relationship" menu item is clicked, a coverage overlay is shown within about 15 ms and the hedge relationship:screen navigation only arrives about 6 s later in all three sessions (click 24 to app:4 at 7830 ms, 25 to app:4 at 7937 ms, 25 to app:4 at 8183 ms), which suggests the route change is gated on work that finishes before the screen opens.
results.fix: Fix: In the Hedging menu, change the "Hedge Relationship" menuitem click handler so it navigates to the hedge relationship screen immediately, and move the blocking load that currently holds the overlay into that screen as an in-place loading state (for example a skeleton on the form fields) instead of waiting for it before the route change.

results.cause: Likely cause: after the "Hedge Relationship" menu item is clicked, a coverage overlay appears and stays up for about 10 s before the hedge relationship screen navigation completes, which suggests the screen waits on work it does before rendering; no network or console error appears in the windows to explain the delay.
results.fix: Fix: In the Hedging menu's "Hedge Relationship" item handler, start the route change to the hedge relationship screen immediately and move its blocking data load into the screen so the loading overlay is dismissed as soon as the screen mounts, then measure the time from the click to the app:4 navigation event.
